q: In a period, the properties of transition elements are very similar in contrast to those of s-block and ____ elements.
e: In a period, the properties of transition elements are very similar in contrast to those of s-block and p-block elements. Transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: These transition elements have typical metallic properties such as malleability, ductility, metallic lustre, and high ____ strength.
e: These transition elements have typical metallic properties such as malleability, ductility, metallic lustre, and high tensile strength. Transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: One cubic centimetre ($1 cm^3$) cube of iron is ____ times heavier than a $1 cm^3$ cube of sodium.
e: One cubic centimetre (1cm3) cube of iron is 8 times heavier than a 1cm3 cube of sodium. 8 is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Transition elements are significantly less reactive than Group ____ metals.
e: Transition elements are significantly less reactive than Group I metals. Transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: For example, nickel and copper do not react with water, or catch fire in the air (oxygen), unlike ____.
e: For example, nickel and copper do not react with water, or catch fire in the air (oxygen), unlike sodium. Sodium is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: In general, transition metals do not ____ readily in the atmosphere.
e: In general, transition metals do not corrode readily in the atmosphere. Transition metals often show variable oxidation states, coloured ions, and catalytic behaviour.

q: But ____ is an exception; it rusts easily.
e: But iron is an exception; it rusts easily. Iron is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Iron combined with non-metal carbon produces an alloy called ____.
e: Iron combined with non-metal carbon produces an alloy called steel. An alloy is a mixture of metals, often harder or more corrosion-resistant than the pure metal.

q: Most transition elements form ____ compounds, whereas Groups 1 and II metals form white compounds.
e: Most transition elements form coloured compounds, whereas Groups 1 and II metals form white compounds. Transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: Most of them can form ions with different charges, so the transition elements show variable ____ states.
e: Most of them can form ions with different charges, so the transition elements show variable oxidation states. Transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: Most transition elements can form ____ ions.
e: Most transition elements can form complex ions. Transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: Compared to 3d series transition metals, alkali metals have a ____ melting point.
e: Compared to 3d series transition metals, alkali metals have a low melting point. Transition metals often show variable oxidation states, coloured ions, and catalytic behaviour.

q: Transition elements typically have incompletely filled d orbitals or readily give rise to ions with partially filled ____ orbitals.
e: Transition elements typically have incompletely filled d orbitals or readily give rise to ions with partially filled d orbitals. Transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, or they form cations with a partly filled d subshell.

q: The ____ oxidation states are more stable at the beginning of the series, i.e., the left side of Mn.
e: The +3 oxidation states are more stable at the beginning of the series,, the left side of Mn. Oxidation state tracks how oxidised an atom is; transition metals often show several values.

q: Towards the end of the series, i.e., the right side of Mn, ____ oxidation states are more stable.
e: Towards the end of the series,, the right side of Mn, +2 oxidation states are more stable. Oxidation state tracks how oxidised an atom is; transition metals often show several values.

q: The elements in the ____ of the series exhibit more oxidation states than those to the left or right.
e: The elements in the middle of the series exhibit more oxidation states than those to the left or right. Oxidation state tracks how oxidised an atom is; transition metals often show several values.

q: The highest oxidation state is ____ for manganese ($^{25}Mn$).
e: The highest oxidation state is +7 for manganese (25Mn). Oxidation state tracks how oxidised an atom is; transition metals often show several values.

q: The ions of chromium, manganese, and iron with the highest oxidation states tend to be good ____ agents.
e: The ions of chromium, manganese, and iron with the highest oxidation states tend to be good oxidising agents. Oxidation state tracks how oxidised an atom is; transition metals often show several values.

q: Vanadium and chromium ions with the lowest oxidation state of +2 are good ____ agents.
e: Vanadium and chromium ions with the lowest oxidation state of +2 are good reducing agents. Oxidation state tracks how oxidised an atom is; transition metals often show several values.

q: Transition metals usually have their highest oxidation states in compounds with high ____ elements such as oxygen and fluorine.
e: Transition metals usually have their highest oxidation states in compounds with high electronegative elements such as oxygen and fluorine. Electronegative: transition metals often show variable oxidation states, coloured ions, and catalytic behaviour.

q: The colour of transition metal compounds is due to the presence of incomplete d orbitals or the presence of ____ electrons.
e: The colour of transition metal compounds is due to the presence of incomplete d orbitals or the presence of unpaired electrons. Transition metals often show variable oxidation states, coloured ions, and catalytic behaviour.

q: The transition metal compounds form coloured ions in an aqueous solution because they absorb part of the visible light and transmit the ____ colour.
e: The transition metal compounds form coloured ions in an aqueous solution because they absorb part of the visible light and transmit the complement colour. Transition metals often show variable oxidation states, coloured ions, and catalytic behaviour.

q: $Sc^{3+}$ and $Zn^{2+}$ ions are ____ because $Sc^{3+}$ ion has completely empty d orbitals, and $Zn^{2+}$ has completely filled d orbitals.
e: Sc3+ and Zn2+ ions are colourless because Sc3+ ion has completely empty d orbitals, and Zn2+ has completely filled d orbitals. The five d orbitals have mostly double-dumbbell shapes and hold up to ten electrons.

q: If the electrons in (n-1)d orbitals are unpaired then it is a ____ substance.
e: If the electrons in (n-1)d orbitals are unpaired then it is a paramagnetic substance. The five d orbitals have mostly double-dumbbell shapes and hold up to ten electrons.

q: If the electrons in (n-1)d orbitals are paired, then it is a ____ substance.
e: If the electrons in (n-1)d orbitals are paired, then it is a diamagnetic substance. The five d orbitals have mostly double-dumbbell shapes and hold up to ten electrons.

q: Substances that are attracted very strongly by the applied magnetic field are said to be ____.
e: Substances that are attracted very strongly by the applied magnetic field are said to be ferromagnetic. Ferromagnetic is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Iron, ____, and nickel are ferromagnetic substances.
e: Iron, cobalt, and nickel are ferromagnetic substances. Cobalt is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Iron is used as a catalyst in the manufacture of ammonia in the ____ process.
e: Iron is used as a catalyst in the manufacture of ammonia in the Haber process. A catalyst speeds or slows a reaction by changing the path, but it is not used up in the overall equation.

q: Vanadium is used in the form of vanadium(V) oxide in the manufacture of sulphuric acid in the ____ process.
e: Vanadium is used in the form of vanadium(V) oxide in the manufacture of sulphuric acid in the Contact process. Contact is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Nickel is used as a catalyst in the ____ of alkenes.
e: Nickel is used as a catalyst in the hydrogenation of alkenes. A catalyst speeds or slows a reaction by changing the path, but it is not used up in the overall equation.

q: Titanium(IV) chloride ($TiCl_4$) is used for the manufacturing of high-density ____ in industries.
e: Titanium(IV) chloride (TiCl4) is used for the manufacturing of high-density polyethene in industries. Polyethene is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: A complex ion is an ion, which has a metal ion at its centre with a number of other molecules or ions ____ it.
e: A complex ion is an ion, which has a metal ion at its centre with a number of other molecules or ions surrounding it. A complex ion has a central metal ion bound to ligands through coordinate bonds.

q: A paramagnetic substance is a substance that has unpaired electrons and shows weak attraction towards the external ____ field.
e: A paramagnetic substance is a substance that has unpaired electrons and shows weak attraction towards the external magnetic field. Magnetic is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: A diamagnetic substance is a substance that has no unpaired electrons and shows slight ____ from the external magnetic field.
e: A diamagnetic substance is a substance that has no unpaired electrons and shows slight repulsion from the external magnetic field. Repulsion is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: A ferromagnetic substance is strongly attracted by the applied magnetic field, and retains its ____ for some time even after the external magnetic field is removed.
e: A ferromagnetic substance is strongly attracted by the applied magnetic field, and retains its magnetisation for some time even after the external magnetic field is removed. Magnetisation is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.
